parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State a similarity and a difference between a down quark and a down antiquark.

markscheme_points.text: similarity: same/equal mass or same/equal (magnitude of) charge or both fundamental (particles)
difference: opposite (sign of) charge or one is matter and the other is antimatter

hints: Hint 1: Think about what makes a particle and its own antiparticle a matching pair - which basic properties must stay the same for them to be partners?
Hint 2: Now think about what must flip sign when you go from matter to antimatter, and recall the charge of a down quark is $-1/3e$.
parts.proper_answer: Similarity: same (rest) mass, same magnitude of charge, both are fundamental particles. Difference: opposite sign of charge, one is matter and the other is antimatter.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What an antiparticle means**
Every fundamental particle has a matching antiparticle. You can picture them as twins with identical size but opposite electrical nature. Mass is a measure of inertia and energy content, so that stays identical.

Step 2: **Apply to down and anti-down**
So for similarity, both have the same rest mass. They also have the same magnitude of charge, $|q| = \frac{1}{3}e$, and both are fundamental with no internal structure.
For difference, all additive quantum numbers reverse. In particular charge reverses: $d$ has $-\frac{1}{3}e$ while $\bar{d}$ has $+\frac{1}{3}e$. In words, one is matter and the other is antimatter.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: state the number of protons and the number of neutrons

markscheme_points.text: number of protons = 13 and number of neutrons = 14

hints: Hint 1: Look carefully at the notation $^{25}_{13}Al$ - remember which number counts protons and which counts total nucleons.
parts.proper_answer: number of protons = 13, number of neutrons = 25 - 13 = 14.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Reading nuclear notation**
In $^{A}_{Z}X$, the lower number $Z$ is the proton number. It tells you the charge and the element. The upper number $A$ is the nucleon number, protons + neutrons together.
Here $Z = 13$, so there are 13 protons.
Neutrons make up the rest: $$N = A - Z = 25 - 13 = 14$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: show that the charge is $2.1 \times 10^{-18}\text{ C}$.
hints: Hint 1: Think about which nucleons actually carry charge in the nucleus and how many of them you found in the last step.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Building nuclear charge**
Neutrons are neutral, so only protons contribute. Each proton carries $+e = +1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.
With 13 protons the total is: $$Q = Z e = 13 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$$ $$Q = 20.8 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C} = 2.08 \times 10^{-18}\text{ C} \approx 2.1 \times 10^{-18}\text{ C}$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The nucleus in (b) is moved along a straight line from point $A$ to point $B$ in a uniform horizontal electric field in a vacuum, as shown in Fig. 8.1.

{{figure:figure_8_1}}

The electric field strength is $11\text{ kV m}^{-1}$.

Calculate the work done to move the charge from $A$ to $B$.
hints: Hint 1: Picture the uniform horizontal field - when the nucleus moves diagonally, which part of the 4.0 cm by 3.0 cm motion is actually along the field lines?
Hint 2: Recall how force on a charge in a uniform field links to field strength, and how work links to force times distance in the direction of the force.
Hint 3: Convert the 4.0 cm parallel distance to metres and the 11 kV m$^{-1}$ to V m$^{-1}$, then combine with $2.1 \times 10^{-18}$ C to get joules.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Only the parallel distance counts**
Work by a constant force is force times distance moved in the direction of the force. The electric force is horizontal because the field is horizontal. The vertical 3.0 cm drop is perpendicular to the force, so it contributes zero work. The horizontal separation is 4.0 cm = 0.040 m. That is the effective distance.

Step 2: **Force on the nucleus**
In a uniform field: $$F = qE$$ Here $q = 2.1 \times 10^{-18}\text{ C}$ and $E = 11\text{ kV m}^{-1} = 11 \times 10^{3}\text{ V m}^{-1}$. So: $$F = 2.1 \times 10^{-18} \times 11 \times 10^{3}$$ $$F = 2.31 \times 10^{-14}\text{ N}$$

Step 3: **Work from A to B**
Now multiply by the distance along the field: $$W = F d = qEd$$ $$W = 2.31 \times 10^{-14} \times 0.040$$ $$W = 9.24 \times 10^{-16}\text{ J} \approx 9.2 \times 10^{-16}\text{ J}$$ This is the energy transferred to move the nucleus against or with the field between A and B.
